topic: Evening back stiffness after a long day

slides.headline: Back stiff by dinner time?
slides.sub: Why long days catch up with your back, and what can help.

slides.title: Why evenings feel stiffer
slides.body: After hours of sitting, standing or driving in similar positions, your back can feel tight and achy by evening. It's often your body asking for a change of position rather than a sign of harm.

slides.title: Break up the day
slides.body: Change position every 30 to 45 minutes. Stand for calls, walk to refill your water and take the stairs. Varying how you load your back through the day often helps more than one long stretch at night.

slides.title: Try a five-minute wind-down
slides.body: Try gentle knee rocks lying on your back, cat-cow on your hands and knees, and a short walk after dinner. Easy movement tends to ease stiffness more than settling straight onto the couch.

slides.title: Where chiropractic can fit
slides.body: Our chiropractors assess how your spine and hips move, then may use hands-on techniques alongside exercises and changes to your daily habits. Adjustments are one tool, not the whole plan.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Back pain with numbness, leg weakness, changes to bladder or bowel control, fever or unexplained weight loss needs prompt medical review. Stiffness that keeps building over weeks is worth assessing.

slides.headline: Want easier evenings?
slides.body: Our chiropractors look at how your back moves through a typical day and build a plan that includes movement you can do at home. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Fine in the morning, stiff as a board by dinner? You're not alone.

Long days of sitting, standing or commuting in similar positions often leave the back feeling tight by evening. Usually that's your body asking for more variety, not a sign something is wrong.

Small changes help: move every 30 to 45 minutes, stand for calls, and finish the day with five minutes of knee rocks, cat-cow and a short walk. Numbness, leg weakness, bladder or bowel changes, fever or unexplained weight loss need prompt medical review.

Our chiropractors at Hybrid Physiotherapy combine hands-on care with exercises and habit changes you can keep up. Book online via the link in bio.
